sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Des Moines, WA?
sections.html:
Des Moines is a King County city on the east shore of Puget Sound in the Seattle metropolitan area, and the Census Bureau estimates 33,032 residents as of July 1, 2025. It is bordered by Federal Way to the south, Kent to the east, SeaTac to the northeast, Burien to the north and Normandy Park to the northwest. That location puts a house within reach of Sea-Tac Airport, the I-5 corridor and the water.

The area was first platted in 1889 by the Des Moines Improvement Company, formed after F. A. Blasher persuaded friends in his home city of Des Moines, Iowa to finance a town on Puget Sound. The city incorporated on June 17, 1959, and annexed the Zenith community in 1982. Sea-Tac Airport lies about 2 miles to the north, and some property in the city has been bought out because of aircraft noise, which is a topic buyers raise.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Des Moines homes?
sections.html:
The median value of an owner-occupied Des Moines home is $597,000, and 60.6 percent of housing is owner-occupied, per Census Bureau QuickFacts. Values marked 2020-2024 come from the American Community Survey.

The mean commute of 30.8 minutes is longer than the 26.4 minutes reported nationally, which is why buyers weigh the new light rail station and highway access so closely.

sections.h2: How do the slopes, neighborhoods and schools in Des Moines affect a sale?
sections.html:
Most of the city rolls down to Puget Sound from about 400 feet along Pacific Highway, which gives many homes a view of the water and Vashon Island. The ravines of Des Moines Creek and Massey Creek cut through that slope. If your lot is near either ravine, expect buyers to ask about drainage, flooding and slope stability, topics the state seller disclosure form raises directly.

  • Marina and downtown: an 838-berth city marina opened in 1970, with a fishing pier and boat launch.
  • Zenith and Woodmont: Saltwater State Park sits in a steep ravine between them and is the most used state park on Puget Sound.
  • Redondo: a boardwalk and aquarium near the Federal Way border.
  • Kent-Des Moines Road area: a park-and-ride with express buses, plus Highline College and a Central Washington University branch.

Most of Des Moines is in Highline Public Schools, with Pacific Middle School and Mount Rainier High School as the local secondary schools. Woodmont and Redondo are in the Federal Way School District, so a few streets share a city but not a district.

Interstate 5, State Routes 99, 509 and 516 serve the city, and the Kent Des Moines light rail station on the 1 Line opened in December 2025 near Highline College. King County Metro buses run to the Burien Transit Center and Kent station, and the park-and-ride at the Kent-Des Moines Road interchange has express service to Seattle and Tacoma. The city also ran a two-month passenger ferry pilot to Bell Harbor Marina in downtown Seattle starting in August 2022.

sections.h2: Does Des Moines regulate short-term rentals and rental licenses?
sections.html:
Yes. A Des Moines owner who rents a home for stays of 30 nights or less needs both a city business license and a short-term rental permit. Applicants provide a notification letter and a signed Good Neighbor Agreement. The city's page lists these rules:

  • A local property representative must be reachable around the clock and respond to complaints within 30 minutes.
  • Only one booking at a time is allowed per dwelling unit, and occupancy follows a city table.
  • No overnight street parking, and the owner must contract for garbage service.
  • Violations can lead to permit denial or revocation and infractions.

Business licenses are filed and renewed annually through FileLocal. A business outside the city needs one only if it earns $4,000 or more a year in Des Moines. If you hold a permit, ask the Community Development office whether it transfers to a buyer, since the answer depends on the permit terms. The office counter is open Tuesday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., at 21630 11th Avenue S, Suite D.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Des Moines house fast?
sections.html:
Sellers in Des Moines usually weigh four approaches against their deadline and the home's condition:

  • List on the market: best for updated homes with water views or close access to the light rail.
  • Sell as-is to an investor: fits deferred repairs, tenant-occupied homes and inherited houses.
  • Sell to a cash buyer: removes loan approval delays, and the closing date can usually be set to your schedule.
  • Sell by owner: saves the agent fee, but you manage disclosure forms and the closing paperwork.

With 39.4 percent of Des Moines households renting, many sales involve a tenant. Check the lease, the notice rules and whether the buyer wants vacant possession before you accept an offer. Compare bids by net proceeds, after the excise tax, any loan payoff and prorated taxes.

sections.h2: What will the excise tax cost on a Des Moines sale?
sections.html:
The state excise tax is graduated under RCW 82.45.060: 1.1 percent of the portion up to $525,000 and 1.28 percent from $525,000 up to $1,525,000. On a $600,000 sale, the state portion is $5,775 on the first $525,000 plus $960 on the next $75,000, which is $6,735 before the local rate is added. The Department of Revenue says the seller usually pays, and the tax is due to the county treasurer where the property is located.

Ask King County for the current excise tax affidavit steps and the combined local rate for Des Moines before closing, and ask your escrow officer to show the tax line on the settlement statement. The Department of Revenue also notes that the first tier moves to $551,000 for sales beginning January 1, 2027.

sections.h2: When are King County property taxes due for a Des Moines owner?
sections.html:
Under RCW 84.56.020, taxes are due April 30, and when the total is $50 or more the owner may pay half by April 30 and the rest by October 31. The October 31, 2026 date has passed, so check the parcel for unpaid second-half tax. The next due date is April 30, 2027. Statements are due to be distributed by March 15 when the county has received the tax roll on time.

Late tax on residential property with four or fewer units carries 9 percent annual interest and no penalties, while other property faces 12 percent plus penalties of 3 percent and then 8 percent. Ask King County Treasury Operations for the exact payoff before closing, since the escrow officer will use that figure to settle the account.

faqs.q: How many people live in Des Moines, WA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 33,032 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 32,888.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Des Moines?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Highline Public Schools. The Woodmont and Redondo neighborhoods are in the Federal Way School District. Confirm the district for the exact address.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Des Moines?
faqs.a: Yes. The owner needs a city business license and a short-term rental permit, plus a notification letter and a signed Good Neighbor Agreement. A local representative must answer complaints within 30 minutes.

faqs.q: How much is the state excise tax on a $600,000 Des Moines sale?
faqs.a: The state portion is $6,735 under the graduated rates: 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent on the next $75,000. A local rate is added on top, and the seller usually pays.

faqs.q: Is Sea-Tac Airport near Des Moines?
faqs.a: Yes. The airport is about 2 miles north of the city, and some Des Moines property has been bought out because of aircraft noise. Ask the county or an agent about noise context for a specific address.
